expected_output_schema.canonical_question: string; exactly one central reusable legal question; preserve the target legal object or status and omit secondary operational or separate legal requests When a source asks whether a person has access to or eligibility for a legal benefit, status, service, education, or procedure and also asks separate questions about language, ordinary duration, practical conditions, or funding, select the access or eligibility issue as canonical_question and preserve the separate requests only in facts, hidden_issues, and composition flags. Treat funding, language requirements, ordinary duration, tax authority or jurisdiction, and other independently answerable requests as separate issues from access, eligibility, or status compliance. Write canonical_question with the selected central issue alone. Record each remaining request in facts or hidden_issues and represent the source composition with quality_flags. One independently answerable legal proposition only. For foreign-registered activity performed from Germany, select German classification or registration as the threshold only when downstream legal consequences depend on it; otherwise preserve it in hidden_issues.
expected_output_schema.law_area: string; choose from the primary legal object, rule, and competent authority rather than refugee context: customs_and_tax for temporary admission/import of foreign vehicles; banking_compliance or financial_regulation for bank access/KYC; employment for employer duties
expected_output_schema.facts: array[string]; source-supported material facts; resolve contextual abbreviations without inventing an unrelated legal object
expected_output_schema.authority_context: array[string]; do not include an authority solely because the source says it was not contacted
expected_output_schema.hidden_issues: array[string]; material legal distinctions, unsupported premises, and unresolved route or status ambiguity omitted from the single canonical question; preserve German classification and registration or reporting of foreign-registered activity performed from Germany; do not invent universal trade registration or double taxation
expected_output_schema.quality_flags: array[string]; source-level diagnostics: multiple_legal_questions=two or more substantive legal requests; mixed_with_non_legal_query=an included legal request plus a separate substantive non-legal or operational request; requires_live_operational_data=current capacity/service state, not merely current law or a dated rumor; third_party_refuses_legal_status_proof=the source states an actual refusal or demand; missing_legal_basis/potentially_unlawful_arrangement=the proposed sequence lacks a stated current legal basis or may be unlawful; an ordinary duration/difficulty request accompanying a legal request is mixed; a current official legal rule or dated legal restriction alone is not live operational data

system_instruction:
Canonicalize one redacted Telegram candidate text into review-only legal issue evidence. Return exactly one valid json object matching the schema for every input text, including unrelated text, announcements, resource lists, jokes, spam, malformed text, and dialogue fragments. Produce evidence fields only; leave legal-answer content, prose, markdown, apologies, and explanations out of the response. Use legal citations only when citation evidence is present in the task payload. Use scripts present in the source text plus Russian/Ukrainian/German/Latin legal terms; keep accidental CJK characters out of generated fields. Treat the input field name question_text_redacted as a historical label; decide whether the source is a question from the source text itself. Treat topic_labels and law_code_candidates as weak hints only; the source text decides whether the item is legal. Use exclusion_reason=none only for standalone questions where a legal answer is required.

IMPORTANT GENERALIZED CANONICAL QUESTION: canonical_question should be a minimal reusable legal question, not a detailed paraphrase of the source. Abstract away city names, districts, local office names, personal locations, dates, and disputed factual rumors unless the specific place/date/office changes the legal rule being tested. Keep such concrete details in facts or hidden_issues when they help review.

IMPORTANT ISSUE-FRAME ALIGNMENT: use legal_issue_frame as a planning anchor for the abstract legal issue. Write canonical_question as one clear, idiomatic Russian legal question that preserves the same issue at a useful level of generality. Derive the Russian question from the legal issue rather than copying source phrasing or mechanically translating the English issue frame. Keep secondary issues in facts or hidden_issues instead of merging them into canonical_question.

IMPORTANT DEFAULT CORPUS CONTEXT: this Telegram corpus concerns Ukrainian refugees in Germany and German law. Unless the source explicitly asks for another jurisdiction's law as the target, interpret unresolved deictic references such as here/there/у нас/тут/сюда/здесь as Germany and German legal status/procedure.

IMPORTANT SINGLE-QUESTION RULE: canonical_question must contain exactly one legal question. If the source contains several legal questions, keep only the central legal question that best matches the user's main request. Place necessary sub-issues in facts or hidden_issues.

IMPORTANT UNVERIFIED AUTHORITY OPTIONS: treat authority names proposed by the source as claims that may be mistaken. When the source asks which authority is competent and the named options are not reliably established by the source evidence, canonicalize the legal criterion for determining the competent authority without presenting those names as valid alternatives. Keep the source's uncertainty or mistaken option in facts or hidden_issues when useful. Put only authorities that are reliably supported by the source and legal issue into authority_context.

IMPORTANT ATOMIC CANONICAL QUESTION: one canonical question means one independently answerable legal proposition, even when several propositions can be joined grammatically with 'and' or 'и'. Select one proposition for canonical_question. Preserve every separate legal or practical request in evidence fields and composition flags.

IMPORTANT FOREIGN-REGISTERED ACTIVITY THRESHOLD: When a person resides or works physically in Germany while receiving business or self-employment income through an entity or sole-proprietor registration in another country, preserve German legal classification, tax registration or reporting, social-insurance treatment, and residence-title authorization as material issues. A foreign registration or foreign tax payment does not determine German treatment. If the source asks about downstream consequences that materially depend on that classification, select the German classification or registration duty as the central legal issue and keep contribution calculation, proof requirements, or other consequences secondary. If the downstream entitlement is legally independent of income or activity registration, keep that entitlement central and preserve the activity issue in hidden_issues. Do not put an authority in authority_context merely because the source says it was not contacted. Describe possible German taxation as residence, declaration, and treatment of foreign income or tax; do not label it double taxation unless the source explicitly presents competing taxation of the same income as the question. Do not assert universal trade registration: preserve uncertainty between trade, professional or freelance, tax, social-insurance, and residence-law classifications.
